system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Central nervous system infections and postinfectious disorders
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: SSPE is a delayed progressive CNS complication of persistent measles virus infection. Years after primary measles, patients develop behavioral or cognitive decline followed by myoclonus, motor deterioration, and characteristic periodic EEG abnormalities; elevated measles antibody in CSF supports the diagnosis.
vignette: A 13-year-old boy develops declining school performance, irritability, and progressive cognitive impairment. Several months later he develops frequent brief myoclonic jerks and worsening gait. He had measles at age 2 years and was never fully vaccinated. EEG shows stereotyped high-voltage periodic complexes occurring at regular intervals. Cerebrospinal fluid has markedly elevated measles-specific antibody.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractor_notes: Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy can cause adolescent myoclonus but does not explain progressive dementia after childhood measles with characteristic periodic complexes and CSF measles antibody.
PML occurs mainly with severe cellular immunosuppression and causes multifocal demyelinating deficits from JC virus rather than this delayed post-measles syndrome.
Wilson disease can cause psychiatric and movement abnormalities but not the characteristic measles history, CSF antibody, and periodic EEG pattern.

Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is generally more acute/subacute and commonly includes prominent psychiatric symptoms, dyskinesias, seizures, and autonomic dysfunction; persistent measles evidence points elsewhere.
key_expl: The combination of remote measles infection, progressive cognitive and behavioral decline, myoclonus, periodic EEG complexes, and elevated CSF measles antibody is classic for SSPE. It reflects persistent measles infection of the CNS with progressive inflammatory and degenerative injury years after the initial infection.
objective: Recognize SSPE from delayed progressive neurocognitive decline and myoclonus after measles infection with characteristic EEG and CSF findings.
